note: User-controlled JS string pattern (32 UTF-16 code units, ending with a backslash) is passed from the RegExp constructor into JSRegExp::initialize.

The pattern is appended into patternText16 (llvh::SmallVector<char16_t,16>): exactly 32 elements are stored, so the vector grows to a heap buffer with capacity == size == 32. The buffer is handed to regex::Regex, which forwards [start, end) to the RegexParser.
While parsing the trailing backslash of the pattern, consume('\\') advances current_ so that current_ == end_ (one past the last pattern element).
Root cause: the word-boundary assertion detection dereferences *current_ without first checking current_ != end_. When the pattern ends with a backslash, this dereferences the cursor at end_.

Sink: out-of-bounds read of the char16_t at end_. For the 32-unit pattern the SmallVector heap allocation (64 bytes) is exactly full, so the 2-byte load lands in the ASAN redzone (heap-buffer-overflow).
